Definition: properly, to rub to pieces or pulverize; intransitively, to disappear as dust; to salt whether internally (to season with salt) or externally (to rub with salt)
BiblicalUsage: Malach means to salt, to season, to rub with salt, and it also means to vanish away like dust. Leviticus 2:13 commands every meat offering to be seasoned with salt, the salt of the covenant of God, and Exodus 30:35 has the holy perfume tempered together, pure and holy. Ezekiel 16:4 says Jerusalem at her birth was not salted at all, and Isaiah 51:6 says the heavens shall vanish away like smoke and the earth wax old like a garment.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word holds covenant and judgment together: salt preserves what God keeps, and the unsalted thing vanishes. My position is that the salt of the covenant in Leviticus 2:13 is the promise behind it all, because what God salts, He keeps.
